searchText: <GuthL> I don't want to do publicity for events here but it seems relevant for this group. Dankrad Feist working on Data Availability Checks for ETH2.0 will present next Tuesday at 5pm UK. Feel free to join https://www.meetup.com/Zero-Knowledge-London/events/270191874/ > I've pushed a short discussion starter on the BLOCKHASH opcode's effect on Stateless Ethereum: https://ethresear.ch/t/the-curious-case-of-blockhash-and-stateless-ethereum/7304 > > Appreciate any feedback, even if it just means this is not a problem 😉 <@425279588009246720> Yeah the BLOCKHASHes are part of the de-facto state. Also if you include in block processing uncle validation, the uncles of the last 8 blocks are also part of the state 🤪 One challenge is, eth2 has its own state root and block hash history accumulator, and it would be nice to not build something that is redundant with it > Also if you include in block processing uncle validation, the uncles of the last 8 blocks are also part of the state 🤪 I'm not completely familiar with how uncles are processed. Briefly checked the YP now and it suggests only the headers are included, so no transaction processing happens. Would the hashes of the uncle headers be valid anywhere? <vbuterin> You need to know what the recent uncles were to ban duplicates <tkstanczak> ----- not blockhash related ----- <tkstanczak> so I am running now a beam sync on mainnet, the way it was envisioned by Jason and Piper (with the background state sync) <tkstanczak> if you would like to try it out I suggest waiting for some 1.8.10 or higher Nethermind version <tkstanczak> I will let you know when we enable it by default on mainnet syncs <tkstanczak> I am now at the stage of collecting ideas to actually make it more efficient (now it may have block gaps on mainnet while syncing) <tkstanczak> any witness format would be immediately usable and I mentioned in the past the naive witness (not really a wtiness, more like a helper) of a list of node hashes for GetNodeData calls <tkstanczak> we may add it to Nethermind as this would be of much smaller size and should be downloadable in milliseconds during the sync if received from peers <tkstanczak> (both the witness and actual data) <tkstanczak> I am thinking of multiple prefetcher in case the witness is not available - txpool, parallel tx executors and so on but so far it seems like it would be more work and complexity than benefit for the users <tkstanczak> to get any usable data to experiment with we would probably need Geth or Parity to support some iind of witnesses <tkstanczak> I think that holding a witness for last 128 blovks or similar would be enough to provide a great experience on the way to iur stateless goal <tkstanczak> one thing, I think, you probably mentioned that, would be useful - to include a list of touched accounts in the witness <tkstanczak> we could do that by using account addresses instead of trie paths and for each trie path we could just include the range of the path from the address hash <tkstanczak> then we do not add extra space overhead (we even save space by using 20 bytes address instead of 32 byte hash) <tkstanczak> and we can allow clients to download the witnessed a build a turbo geth style indocea for accounts <tkstanczak> *indices

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content:
> I've pushed a short discussion starter on the BLOCKHASH opcode's effect on Stateless Ethereum: https://ethresear.ch/t/the-curious-case-of-blockhash-and-stateless-ethereum/7304
> 
> Appreciate any feedback, even if it just means this is not a problem 😉
<@425279588009246720> Yeah the BLOCKHASHes are part of the de-facto state. Also if you include in block processing uncle validation, the uncles of the last 8 blocks are also part of the state 🤪

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: One challenge is, eth2 has its own state root and block hash history accumulator, and it would be nice to not build something that is redundant with it

excerpts.author: axic3354
excerpts.content:
> Also if you include in block processing uncle validation, the uncles of the last 8 blocks are also part of the state 🤪

I'm not completely familiar with how uncles are processed. Briefly checked the YP now and it suggests only the headers are included, so no transaction processing happens. Would the hashes of the uncle headers be valid anywhere?
